components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Solid signal-red CTA with a trimmed bottom-right corner; used for phone/directions actions.
components.css: .ds-btn { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 0.5rem; font-family: 'Barlow', sans-serif; font-weight: 700; font-size: 1rem; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.02em; padding: 0.9rem 1.6rem; border: 2px solid transparent; clip-path: polygon(0 0, 100% 0, 100% calc(100% - 14px), calc(100% - 14px) 100%, 0 100%); transition: background-color 160ms ease, color 160ms ease, border-color 160ms ease, transform 160ms ease; cursor: pointer; } .ds-btn:active { transform: translateY(1px); } .ds-btn-primary { background: #d82629; color: #ffffff; border-color: #d82629; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #a91d20; border-color: #a91d20; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid #d82629; outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Kuruma Booking Button
components.description: Deliberately non-brand blue booking CTA, reserved only for KurumaWorks booking links.
components.html: Book Us on Kuruma
components.css: .ds-btn-kuruma { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; font-family: 'Barlow', sans-serif; font-weight: 700; font-size: 1rem; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.02em; padding: 0.9rem 1.6rem; border: 2px solid #2663eb; clip-path: polygon(0 0, 100% 0, 100% calc(100% - 14px), calc(100% - 14px) 100%, 0 100%); background: #2663eb; color: #ffffff; transition: background-color 160ms ease, color 160ms ease; } .ds-btn-kuruma:hover { background: #ffffff; color: #2663eb; } .ds-btn-kuruma:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid #d82629; outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Tag Chip

components.css: .ds-chip { display: inline-block; background: #d82629; color: #ffffff; font-family: 'Barlow', sans-serif; font-weight: 700; font-size: 0.7rem; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.08em; padding: 0.25rem 0.55rem; }

components.name: Hero Letter-Stack
components.description: Two-tone animated Anton letter reveal; ink word then red word, staggered 140ms, disabled under prefers-reduced-motion.
components.css: .ds-hero-title { font-family: 'Anton', 'Arial Narrow', sans-serif; font-size: clamp(3rem, 9vw, 6rem); line-height: 0.92; letter-spacing: -0.01em; text-transform: uppercase; } .ds-hero-title span { display: block; animation: ds-sign-letter 640ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1) both; } .ds-hero-word-ink { color: #1a1613; } .ds-hero-word-red { color: #d82629; animation-delay: 140ms; } @keyframes ds-sign-letter { from { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(0.4em); } to { opacity: 1; transform: translateY(0); } } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-hero-title span { animation: none; } }

narrative.overview: The real hand-lettered vinyl banner on the shop wall (visible in public/outside.webp) is the whole design system, not a reference for one. Everything on the page is built the way a sign shop builds a banner: bold, blocky, even-stroke lettering; a strict flat ink palette; and edges cut, not rounded. The build refuses the tire-shop category default of soft SaaS gradients, rounded pill buttons, and icon-grid feature blocks; there are zero gradients, zero box-shadows, and zero glassmorphism anywhere in the shipped CSS. The system is loud where it needs to be (the hero letter-stack, the red ink blocks) and gets out of the way everywhere else: white and warm concrete grounds, hairline rules standing in for grommet lines, and Barlow doing plain, legible work at UI scale. Signal red is rationed to ink blocks -- hero accents, tags, dividers, CTA panels -- not washed across backgrounds.
keyCharacteristics: Flat ink blocks in red, black, and white; no gradients, no glass, no soft drop shadows anywhere in the build.
A single recurring trimmed-corner "cut vinyl" notch (clip-path) unifies buttons, banners, and panels.
Anton for all display lettering (always uppercase, tight leading); Barlow for everything read at body/UI size.
The real shop photo (outside.webp) is bled to the hero edge as proof-of-place, never used as a background wash.

rules.name: The Kuruma-Blue Separation Rule
rules.body: KurumaWorks blue (#2663eb) is a foreign, non-brand color by design, reserved only for the external booking action (.btn-kuruma). It must never be blended into the red/ink/concrete palette or reused for any other purpose -- its visual distinctness is the point, marking "this leaves the shop's own brand voice."

rules.name: The Rationed Red Rule
rules.body: Signal red reads as ink, not wallpaper: it appears in bounded blocks (buttons, tags, banner strips, alternating why-panels) against white or concrete grounds, never as a full-bleed background wash.

rules.name: The All-Caps Display Rule
rules.body: Anton is never set in mixed case; every instance in the build is uppercase, matching cut-vinyl sign lettering.

rules.name: The No-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Surfaces never lift with a shadow. Separation between elements is carried by flat color contrast and hairline rules only.

dos: Do keep all display type (Anton) uppercase; it is never set in mixed or lower case anywhere in the build.
Do use the single-corner clip-path notch (14px) as the one recurring signature silhouette for buttons, banners, and accent panels -- not a generic rounded radius.
Do ration signal red to bounded ink blocks (buttons, tags, banners, alternating panels), not full backgrounds.
Do keep KurumaWorks blue (#2663eb) confined to booking CTAs only, visually distinct from the shop's own palette everywhere else.
donts: Don't add gradients, glassmorphism, or box-shadow anywhere; the system is flat by commitment, and every current surface ships with zero shadow declarations.
Don't round any corner; the only cut allowed is the single trimmed-corner clip-path notch or, for the hero emblem, a true circle.
Don't blend KurumaWorks blue into the brand palette or reuse it outside .btn-kuruma.

Don't treat --red-deep (#6e1315) as an active system color: it is declared in :root but not used anywhere in the shipped build. Carry it as a reserved/unused token rather than inventing a use for it or removing it silently.
